scope_contract.N001: All four parts of Theorem1, with source definitions and all ranks >=1.
scope_contract.N003: All eight numbered results, restricting general group results to finite groups and keeping n>=7 for symmetric-group classifications; Theorem3.1 strong-independence consequence included.
scope_contract.N008: All principal new geometric results, finite Theorem 2.1 with explicit infinite correction, all subsidiary numbered statements except retained Gaschütz4.1, and residue/kernel consequences; source finite-p-group context retained.
scope_contract.infinite_scope: Finite rank only. E0,R(b),E1-E3 and the residue/kernel consequences allow infinite groups where stated. E4 gives a corrected relative-generation theorem; numerical mu bounds and p-group classifications are finite.
scope_contract.not_assumed_for_N008: Initial flag transitivity or residual connectedness; E0 proves flag transitivity and R(b) needs no G2.
scope_contract.fixed_action_convention: Typed subgroup families with their specified group actions and fixed quotient map; no unproved automorphism-lifting or orbit-count correspondence.

targets.full_source_formulation_normalized: For every inductively minimal finite pair (Gamma,G), the pair is RWPRI and has properties (2T)_1 and (IP)_2.
targets.adapter_argument: B97 plus D identifies the tree; I supplies all three residual/local properties.
targets.component_review: two-paper manuscript independently reviewed under the declared scope

targets.full_source_formulation_normalized: An inductively minimal pair of even rank is PRI.
targets.adapter_argument: The tree has an odd number of vertices, so every cut is unbalanced.
targets.component_review: two-paper manuscript independently reviewed under the declared scope

targets.full_source_formulation_normalized: For an inductively minimal pair, failure of PRI implies QPRI; failure of PRI occurs exactly when the connected diagram has a middle (a nonend whose deletion components have equal cardinality).
targets.adapter_argument: A diagram middle is exactly a balanced nonleaf cut; O identifies its unique subgroup chain.
targets.interpretive_note: The printed phrase "this is the case" is read as failure of PRI, as its proof confirms. PRI pairs are also QPRI under the source definition. The manuscript states the stronger unambiguous profile. A middle explicitly requires at least two deletion components; the one-vertex diagram has none.
targets.component_review: two-paper manuscript independently reviewed under the declared scope

targets.full_source_formulation_normalized: An inductively minimal pair is RPRI if and only if its diagram is a complete graph.
targets.adapter_argument: Stars have only leaf cuts in their residues; every nonstar contains the obstructing three-edge path.
targets.component_review: two-paper manuscript independently reviewed under the declared scope

targets.full_source_formulation_normalized: For a normal subgroup N of G, mu(G) <= mu(G/N)+mu_prime(N). If N is abelian, mu(G) <= mu(G/N)+mu_prime_G(N), with G acting on N by conjugation. The printed source says a group; this contract takes finite G.
targets.adapter_argument: Choose a quotient-minimal subfamily and replace every remaining generator by an element of N; for abelian N conjugators can be taken in the chosen lift.
targets.component_review: two-paper manuscript independently reviewed under the declared scope

targets.full_source_formulation_normalized: For n >= 7, every independent generating set S of S_n of size n-1 is S(T), the edge transpositions of a labelled tree T, or {s} union {(s t)^epsilon(t): t in S(T) except s}, where s in S(T) and epsilon(t) in {+1,-1}. Conversely every set of either form is an independent generating set of S_n.
targets.adapter_argument: M removes the imprimitive case; orbit-crossing edges yield a tree; F limits each generator support; P gives the converse.
targets.component_review: two-paper manuscript independently reviewed under the declared scope

targets.full_source_formulation_normalized: For the two families of Theorem 2.1, the numbers of actual unordered generating sets are n^(n-2) and (n-1)n^(n-2), respectively; identifying each 3-cycle with its inverse changes the second count to binomial(n,2)(n-1)^(n-3). Degree n >= 7 is inherited from that theorem.
targets.common_result: F, P, M, E; B3 count adapter
targets.adapter_argument: Actual twisted sets recover a unique distinguished-edge tree by multiplication by the unique odd member; inverse identification contracts that edge.
targets.component_review: two-paper manuscript independently reviewed under the declared scope

targets.full_source_formulation_normalized: For n >= 7 every independent generating set (s_i:i in I) of S_n of size n-1 is strongly independent: with G_J=<s_i:i not in J>, G_J intersect G_K = G_(J union K) for all J,K subsets of I.
targets.adapter_argument: Recognize the two markings and apply their exact subset formulas, including the empty subset.
targets.component_review: two-paper manuscript independently reviewed under the declared scope

targets.full_source_formulation_normalized: For n >= 7 and B <= S_n, mu(S_n,B)=n-1 implies B=1.
targets.adapter_argument: Maximal omission subgroups contain B; a leaf cut forces a fixed point and excludes the half-swapping coset at a balanced cut.
targets.component_review: two-paper manuscript independently reviewed under the declared scope

targets.source_reference: Theorem 3.1 and its immediately stated consequence
targets.full_source_formulation_normalized: A source coset geometry for G with Borel B has rank <= mu_prime(G,B). An RWPRI source coset geometry has rank <= mu(G,B), and choices s_i in H_(I minus {i}) outside H_i form a strongly independent relative generating family. The printed source does not impose finite G; this contract takes finite G.
targets.adapter_argument: Panel choices give relative independence; a residual maximal subgroup induction gives every parabolic and strong independence.
targets.component_review: two-paper manuscript independently reviewed under the declared scope

targets.full_source_formulation_normalized: For n >= 7 there is a bijection between independent generating sets of S_n of size n-1, modulo simultaneous conjugation and inversion of individual generators, and RWPRI coset geometries for S_n of rank n-1. The specified group action is retained and set order/type labels may be renamed.
targets.common_result: F, P, O, R, M, E, G
targets.adapter_argument: F completes cut flags; parity is adjusted by the distinguished transposition; G proves every residue primitive in some type, and cyclic panels give uniqueness.
targets.component_review: two-paper manuscript independently reviewed under the declared scope

targets.full_source_formulation_normalized: For n >= 7 every source coset geometry of S_n of rank n-1 is RWPRI, without an initial RWPRI hypothesis.
targets.common_result: F, P, O, R, M, E, G
targets.adapter_argument: Only one balanced parabolic can enlarge; a second cut blocks half interchange in every panel; (G2) recovers all parabolics from those panels.
targets.component_review: two-paper manuscript independently reviewed under the declared scope

targets.full_source_formulation_normalized: For B<=G and Phi=Phi(G), a family (s_i) is an independent generating family of G relative to B iff (Phi s_i) is an independent generating family of G/Phi relative to BPhi/Phi.
targets.adapter_argument: **Corollary C1 — N008 Theorem 2.1, finite specialization and corrected infinite converse.** Relative independent generating families in a finite group descend to and lift from its Frattini quotient, relative to the image of \(B\). This is E4. Its printed unrestricted infinite converse is replaced by E4's explicit additional hypothesis and the preceding counterexample.
targets.component_review: N008 extension independently reviewed under its corrected main-result contract
targets.correction: Finite specialization retained; unrestricted infinite converse false. E4 supplies a sufficient infinite condition and the explicit Prüfer-product counterexample is in the body.

targets.full_source_formulation_normalized: A firm RWPRI coset geometry satisfies Phi(G)<=H_i for every type i, including infinite G.
targets.adapter_argument: **Corollary C2 — N008 Theorem 3.1.** In any finite-rank firm RWPRI coset geometry, \(\Phi(G)\leq H_i\) for every type, including infinite groups. Lemma E0 and firmness give the lattice hypotheses, and E2 yields the stronger \(\Phi(G)\leq B\).
targets.component_review: N008 extension independently reviewed under its corrected main-result contract

targets.full_source_formulation_normalized: If N is normal in G and N<=H_i for every type of a coset pregeometry, that pregeometry is isomorphic to the coset pregeometry (G/N,(H_i/N)).
targets.adapter_argument: **Corollary C3 — N008 Proposition 3.2.** A coset pregeometry whose type subgroups contain \(N\unlhd G\) is isomorphic to the pregeometry of their images in \(G/N\). This is E3 without any flag-transitivity assumption.
targets.component_review: N008 extension independently reviewed under its corrected main-result contract

targets.full_source_formulation_normalized: A firm RWPRI coset geometry (G,(H_i)) is isomorphic to (G/Phi(G),(H_i/Phi(G))).
targets.adapter_argument: **Corollary C4 — N008 Corollary 3.3.** Every firm RWPRI coset geometry is isomorphic to its Frattini-quotient coset geometry. Combine C2 with E3.
targets.component_review: N008 extension independently reviewed under its corrected main-result contract

targets.full_source_formulation_normalized: Every firm RWPRI geometry is isomorphic to a firm RWPRI geometry for a Frattini-free group.
targets.adapter_argument: **Corollary C5 — N008 Theorem 3.4.** Every firm RWPRI geometry is isomorphic to one for a Frattini-free group. Apply C4 and the maximal-subgroup correspondence following E3. Quotient and pullback give the fixed-indexed-family bijection motivating the paper.
targets.component_review: N008 extension independently reviewed under its corrected main-result contract

targets.full_source_formulation_normalized: A rank-two coset pregeometry (G,(H_1,H_2)) is a direct sum iff H_1 H_2=G.
targets.adapter_argument: **Corollary C6 — N008 Proposition 3.5.** A rank-two coset pregeometry is a direct sum exactly when \(H_1H_2=G\). This is the coset-product calculation after E5, with no finiteness or normality assumption.
targets.component_review: N008 extension independently reviewed under its corrected main-result contract

targets.full_source_formulation_normalized: For proper U,W<F_p^k with W not contained in U, if U is maximal and U intersect W is maximal in U, then W is maximal in F_p^k.
targets.adapter_argument: **Corollary C7 — N008 Lemma 3.6.** If \(U,W<\mathbb F_p^k\), \(W\not\subseteq U\), \(U\) is maximal and \(U\cap W\) is maximal in \(U\), then \(W\) is maximal in \(\mathbb F_p^k\). This is the dimension calculation after E5.
targets.component_review: N008 extension independently reviewed under its corrected main-result contract

targets.full_source_formulation_normalized: A firm coset geometry of a finite p-group is RWPRI iff it is RPRI.
targets.common_result: E0,E2,E3,E5 and Theorem R(b) of this integrated manuscript
targets.adapter_argument: **Corollary C8 — N008 Proposition 3.7.** A firm coset geometry of a finite p-group is RWPRI if and only if it is RPRI. E5 proves the nontrivial implication; the converse is immediate from the definitions.
targets.component_review: N008 extension independently reviewed under its corrected main-result contract

targets.full_source_formulation_normalized: A firm RWPRI coset geometry of a p-group is a direct sum of primitive rank-one geometries. The source section fixes finite p-groups, although this theorem sentence omits the word finite.
targets.common_result: E0,E2,E3,E5 and Theorem R(b) of this integrated manuscript
targets.adapter_argument: **Corollary C9 — N008 Theorem 3.8, finite-p-group context.** Every firm RWPRI coset geometry of a finite p-group is a direct sum of primitive geometries of rank one. This is E5; each summand has exactly \(p\) points.
targets.component_review: N008 extension independently reviewed under its corrected main-result contract
targets.scope_note: The printed theorem sentence omits finite; its section explicitly begins with finite p-groups. No arbitrary infinite-p-group theorem is asserted.

targets.full_source_formulation_normalized: For every residue at a flag of type J, Phi(H_J)<=H_J intersect H_i for every remaining type i; this is necessary, not sufficient.
targets.adapter_argument: **Corollary C10 — N008 §4.2.** For each standard flag of type \(J\), \(\Phi(H_J)\) must lie in every \(H_J\cap H_i\), \(i\notin J\). This is (6.7), derived by applying E2 in each residue.
targets.component_review: N008 extension independently reviewed under its corrected main-result contract

targets.full_source_formulation_normalized: The largest normal subgroup of G contained in B is core_G(B)=intersection_i core_G(H_i); quotienting yields the faithful coset action, and for firm RWPRI geometries this kernel contains Phi(G). The separately cited Archer2004 classification at the end of this section is retained, not newly proved.
targets.adapter_argument: **Corollary C11 — N008 §4.3, action-kernel assertion.** The largest normal subgroup of \(G\) contained in the Borel is \(\operatorname{core}_G(B)=\bigcap_i\operatorname{core}_G(H_i)\). Quotienting by it preserves the geometry and makes the action faithful; for firm RWPRI geometries it contains \(\Phi(G)\). This is (6.4), E3 and E2.
targets.component_review: N008 extension independently reviewed under its corrected main-result contract

retained_background.statement: Inductively minimal rank-r pairs are thin and residually connected, with group S_(r+1); their connected diagrams have no induced cycles longer than three, every edge in exactly one maximal clique, and every vertex in one or two maximal cliques; conversely each permitted connected diagram determines one pair up to isomorphism.
retained_background.reference: Buekenhout-Cara-Dehon 1997, Mostly Finite Geometries, pp185-190, as restated in N001 Lemma1 and following paragraph
retained_background.not_targeted: The 1997 classification itself is outside this intake.

retained_background.statement: Every independent family in S_m has size <=m-1; every independent family of size m-1 generates S_m.
retained_background.reference: Whiston 2000, Journal of Algebra232,255-268; source recital N003 p3
retained_background.read_limit: N003 recital read; original Whiston proof not independently read in this assembly.
retained_background.normalization: N003 recital says equality iff generation; only the required extremal-size => generation direction is retained, not a false assertion that all minimal generating sets have maximal size.

retained_background.statement: For n>=7 an omission subgroup of an independent (n-1)-element generating family in S_n is intransitive, transitive imprimitive with two-point blocks, or A_n.
retained_background.reference: N003 p4 consequence explicitly attributed to Whiston [8]

retained_background.statement: The number of trees on a specified labelled m-point set is m^(m-2).
retained_background.reference: Classical formula, also invoked in N003 Corollary2.2

retained_background.statement: The source (G1)-(G3) criterion and residue/coset correspondence; RWPRI equivalence to (G4). All conditions are restated in manuscript section1.
retained_background.reference: N003 author manuscript pp7-8; Buekenhout1995, Buekenhout-Hermand1991, Tits1974 as cited there.
retained_background.read_limit: The exact criterion in N003 has been read; the earlier reference books/articles were not independently acquired for this assembly.

retained_background.statement: Every automorphism of S_n is inner for n>=7.
retained_background.reference: Classical symmetric-group automorphism fact, used only if group-geometry isomorphisms allow automorphisms of the specified action.
retained_background.alternative: The source conjugate-coset-data convention avoids this additional isomorphism convention.

retained_background.statement: Elementary finite group and permutation theory, vector spaces over F2, sign, finite maxima, primitive action iff maximal point stabilizer; all nontrivial forest, parity, module and overgroup arguments are expanded in manuscript.
For finite p-groups P, P/Phi(P) is an elementary abelian p-group.
Every nonempty partially ordered set whose chains have upper bounds has a maximal element.
retained_background.finite_branch: For finite groups the proof explicitly selects a proper overgroup of largest order and does not need Zorn.

retained_background.statement: A finite Frattini-free F with socle S=A times D (abelian and nonabelian simple factors respectively) has F=A semidirect K, K<=Aut(S)=Aut(A) times Aut(D), D=Inn(S)<=K, and K acts semisimply on A; the intersection of maximal K-invariant subgroups of A is trivial.
retained_background.reference: N008 Theorem 4.1 p175, quoting Gaschütz, Math.Z.58(1953),160-170

retained_background.statement: The earlier reduction, cited in N008 section4.3, of RPRI geometries that are not direct sums to primitive group actions after removing the action kernel.
retained_background.reference: C.Archer, Direct sum decomposition of geometries based on maximal subgroups, J.Geometry79(2004),12-18
